title: India Raises Illinois Temple Plot With US as Manifesto Details Emerge
excerpt: The MEA called the alleged plot "deeply concerning" and said it is in touch with US authorities and the Indian community, as reports detailed a manifesto describing Indians as "subhuman."
body:
• India's Ministry of External Affairs called the alleged Illinois temple plot "deeply concerning" and said it is in touch with US authorities and the Indian community, ThePrint reported.
  • The accused, Alexandros Paporakis, 19, allegedly wrote a manifesto describing Indians as "subhuman" and "parasites," according to The Indian Express.
  • His rifle jammed during the alleged attempt, and Nazi symbols and swastikas were reported found in his bedroom.
  • Paporakis has pleaded not guilty and is held on a $10 million bond; his next hearing is October 16.

India has formally raised the alleged plot to attack a Hindu temple in Illinois with the United States, calling it "deeply concerning," as new reporting detailed a manifesto in which the accused teenager allegedly described Indians as "subhuman." The Ministry of External Affairs said it is in touch with US authorities and with the Indian community in Illinois, according to ThePrint — New Delhi's first on-record response to a case we reported yesterday, when the 19-year-old was charged over the alleged plot near Chicago.

What the Manifesto Allegedly Says

The Indian Express reported that Alexandros Paporakis wrote in a manifesto about killing Indians, describing them as "subhuman" and "parasites." The Times of India reported the document ran to eight pages. Investigators also found Nazi symbols and swastikas in his bedroom, according to the reports — a combination that has sharpened the case's profile from a local weapons arrest into a hate-crime story watched in two capitals.

https://x.com/CNNnews18/status/2110549986349920625

According to the reports, the plot failed at the moment it was attempted: the assault-style rifle Paporakis had brought jammed. A tip from an acquaintance and GPS data from an ankle monitor he was already wearing helped federal agents piece together the plan, the reports said.

New Delhi's Response

The MEA's intervention matters for what it signals. India does not comment on every US criminal case involving its diaspora; a public statement, contact with US authorities, and outreach to the Indian community in Illinois mark this as a case Delhi is tracking at the diplomatic level. ThePrint reported the ministry framed the incident within growing concern about racist hostility and anti-India hate in the US.

That concern has a local address. Hindu temples in the Chicago suburbs serve congregations that draw thousands of families on festival weekends — and Diwali is days away. Community leaders now face the practical question behind the diplomatic one: what security looks like at a temple door during the busiest week of the Hindu calendar.

What Happens Next

Paporakis has pleaded not guilty and is being held on a $10 million bond. His next court hearing is scheduled for October 16, when prosecutors are expected to lay out more of the evidence, potentially including the manifesto itself. Until then, the document's contents rest on law-enforcement accounts reported by Indian outlets; the defence has not publicly addressed them.

For the congregation at the centre of the alleged plot, the sequence is stark: a jammed rifle, an ankle monitor's data trail, and a tip from someone who knew him are, on the reported facts, all that stood between a plan on paper and a mass shooting at a place of worship.
